transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (ArcadiaPay CTO), Marcus Vale (Lead Backend Eng), Priya Sharma (Security Architect), Evan Cho (PM)

Summary: quick discovery to understand ArcadiaPay's integration needs for payments fraud detection + conversational support. Primarily interested in integration patterns (SDK vs HTTP proxy), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, quotas/rate-limits, and observability hooks.

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for making time, this is Sofia from Redwood, i'll pass to Daniel for the tech bits after quick intros.
00:12 Lena: Thanks, Lena here, CTO at ArcadiaPay. We're evaluating hosted inference vs Dedicated or full private for regulatory reasons. main use cases are realtime chat assistants for merchants and a fraud classification scoring service.
00:28 Marcus: Hi team, Marcus. we're on k8s, run services in GCP, have an API gateway in front that does IP allow-listing and some mutating auth headers. latency target is 100-200ms for chat generation  p50 ideally.
00:42 Daniel: great, thanks. just to confirm: your throughput for the fraud scorer — what's steady QPS and burst?
00:50 Marcus: steady is ~60 qps across instances, bursts to 250 qps during peak times. average prompt size for scoring is small, like 200-300 tokens; chat prompts get bigger, 400-800 tokens.
01:05 Priya: quick security note — we need SOC2, single-tenant audit logs, SSO (okta), and KMS integration for any encryption of customer keys. Also data residency for EU customers.
01:20 Sofia: perfect, all typical asks. Redwood supports SSO/SAML and KMS/HSM for Private customers; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS in many cases — we have a security pack that i'll share.
01:33 Daniel: from an integration perspective we have two common patterns: 1) direct use of the Redwood REST/SDKs (python/node) which gives you streaming and tooling like function calls; 2) route traffic through your gateway/proxy where the proxy forwards requests to Redwood. both are supported.
01:50 Marcus: if we proxy all traffic through our gateway can we still keep per-route quotas? we want to enforce rate-limits upstream.
02:00 Daniel: yes. rate-limits are enforced at the Redwood account/route level, but you can set per-route quotas and our API keys can be scoped. If you proxy, you'd typically forward the original route header and we can apply route matching on that header. note there can be slight latency added from extra network hop.
02:20 Marcus: understood. curious about batching — you mentioned automatic batching in the docs. how does that interact with latency goals?
02:30 Daniel: good question. our runtime does continuous batching on the server side: for short requests it can batch to improve throughput and lower cost, but we have latency SLO controls — you can set max-wait thresholds so critical routes flush immediately. in Dedicated you can tune batching aggressiveness per model pool.
02:55 Lena: and KV cache — will sessions for chat keep KV cache across requests if we use multiple pods? we have a microservices pattern where requests could hit any instance.
03:10 Daniel: yes — KV cache is maintained in memory per serving node, but for Multi-node you can pin users to a session or use our sticky-routing option. for Dedicated we support a shared KV cache layer with fast lookups; small note — sometimes transcripts show up as K-V cash in early docs (laughs).
03:28 (laughter)
03:34 Evan: on the developer side, we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in a few services. do you have prebuilt connectors or examples?
03:42 Daniel: yes, we have sample LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters in the SDK repo. examples show both sync calls and streaming. common pattern is to use the Redwood SDK as the LLM provider in chain-of-thought workflows. we'll share a short notebook.
03:55 Marcus: what's the SDK like for Node/Python? we already have a typescript codebase for the chat UI.
04:01 Daniel: SDKs are lightweight: python and node both, support streaming, function-calling, and you can plug them into LangChain readily. we also have a simple HTTP shim if you only want fetch/curl.
04:15 Priya: observability — we need per-request tracing and metrics. can Redwood emit spans to Jaeger and metrics to Prometheus? we also want token-level cost breakdowns per route.
04:30 Daniel: yes on both: we emit structured logs and have tracing hooks; you can forward traces to Jaeger or OpenTelemetry collectors. Prometheus metrics include per-route rps, latency histograms, and token counts. the Console also shows token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost.
04:52 Priya: are audit logs immutable? our auditors require tamper-evident logs.
04:58 Sofia: for Dedicated and Private we expose append-only audit logs and longer retention options, and we can integrate with your SIEM. i'll attach the security whitepaper which details retention and immutability guarantees.
05:12 Marcus: what's the default rate limit on Hosted? we need to ensure no noisy neighbor issues.
05:18 Sofia: Hosted has default quotas but they scale with plan; we can create rate-limits per route and per API key, and Dedicated gives you reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbor. we can also set burst policies for scheduled peak windows.
05:34 Marcus: latency numbers — do you have benchmarks for p50/p95 on Hosted vs Dedicated for similar models?
05:42 Daniel: we have perf profiles in the model catalog. hosted p50 for a 2k-context model is typically 80-120ms depending on model. Dedicated will be lower and more consistent; we can run a quick benchmark as a pilot.
05:58 Evan: regarding deployment flow, can we pin a model version and do canary rollouts?
06:04 Daniel: yes — rollouts are supported: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies if the canary fails. the Console exposes per-canary metrics.
06:15 Lena: ok we've got a compliance threshold: if hosted cannot meet KMS / audit requirements for EU data we may need Dedicated with VPC. what's the migration story?
06:28 Sofia: migration is straightforward; same API surface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. you can pin model versions and move traffic. Dedicated gives you a private pool and can be deployed in a VPC in your cloud account; Private adds a local control plane option. Daniel can share an ops playbook.
06:45 Daniel: i'll add that playbook to the follow ups. it includes network diagrams, KMS patterns, and example terraform snippets.
06:52 Marcus: for the HTTP gateway pattern: do you recommend we terminate TLS at our gateway and forward to Redwood over mTLS?
06:58 Daniel: yes, that's a common pattern. we support mTLS from your proxy to Redwood endpoints; alternatively you can use API keys and IP allow-listing. for Dedicated/Private you can also set up direct peering.
07:12 Priya: anything we should be aware of with LangChain usage? we have chain-of-thought that spawns many short calls; batching could combine them and change behavior.
07:24 Daniel: good catch — batching can affect ordering / timing. we provide flush controls and you can set critical chains to low-latency routes. also function-calling reduces token churn for structured outputs.
07:40 Evan: do you have examples of embedding + LlamaIndex retrieval pipelines?
07:45 Daniel: yes, we have an embeddings SDK plus LlamaIndex connector samples. typical pattern: store embeddings in your vector DB (we also integrate with common DBs) and call Redwood for text generation. we'll share a quickstart notebook.
07:58 (brief silence)
08:02 Sofia: ok last thing: what's the pilot look like? we propose sandbox tenant, run a fortnight benchmark with your traffic patterns (simulate bursts), share a cost/latency report, and then decide Hosted vs Dedicated.
08:17 Lena: that sounds good. budget and timeline: we need a pilot decision in 3 weeks to align with Q1 rollouts.
08:24 Sofia: perfect — we can hit that timeline. to recap next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs, Daniel will prep LangChain examples and ops playbook, and we'll provision a sandbox for you to test.
08:39 Marcus: thanks everyone. we'll collect traffic profiles and share with Daniel.
08:45 Sofia: thanks all, meeting end.
